intro: Moldova lies between Romania and Ukraine and has been fought over by empires for centuries. Independent since 1991, it is split by a breakaway region and is working to join the European Union.

chapters.title: Moldavia and empires
text: Much of today's Moldova was part of the medieval Principality of Moldavia, whose prince Stephen the Great fought the Ottomans in the late 1400s. Moldavia later became an Ottoman vassal.
In 1812 Russia took the eastern half, called Bessarabia. It joined Romania in 1918, but the Soviet Union seized it in 1940, deporting tens of thousands of people.

chapters.title: Independence and Transnistria
text: Moldova declared independence on 27 August 1991. In 1992 a short war broke out with Transnistria, a strip east of the Dniester River whose Russian-speaking leaders wanted to stay close to Russia. Transnistria has run itself ever since, unrecognised by any UN member, with Russian troops stationed there.
Moldova became a candidate to join the EU in 2022, and in 2024 voters narrowly backed EU membership in a referendum.

chapters.title: Moldova today
text: President Maia Sandu, the first woman in the job, has led a push towards the EU, while Russia tries to keep its influence. Moldova took in many Ukrainian refugees in 2022.

timeline.title: Stephen the Great
timeline.text: He begins his long reign over Moldavia.

timeline.title: Soviet annexation
timeline.text: The Soviet Union takes the region.

timeline.title: EU candidate
timeline.text: Moldova starts the path to membership.

keyTerms.meaning: A state that is under another state's control.
An area that has declared itself independent without international recognition.
